html:
Portobelo is a port on the Caribbean coast of Panama, founded in 1597. For over a century it held the great fairs where the silver of Peru was traded for European goods brought by the Spanish fleets.

When the galleons came from Spain, merchants from Lima arrived from Panama with silver by mule train. For a few weeks the small, unhealthy town filled with traders, and huge sums changed hands. The rest of the year it was nearly empty. Forts guarded the bay.

Pirates and enemies attacked it again and again: Henry Morgan in 1668 and the British admiral Edward Vernon in 1739, who destroyed its forts. After that, Spain sent ships around Cape Horn instead, and the fairs ended. Its ruined forts are a World Heritage Site. The town keeps strong Afro-Panamanian traditions in Panama, whose crossing later carried the Panama Railroad.
